evidence_items.publisher: arXiv (Zhu et al., incl. Stanford, Berkeley, UK AISI researchers)

receipt.public_excerpt: many agentic benchmarks have issues in task setup or reward design. For example, SWE-bench Verified uses insufficient test cases, while TAU-bench counts empty responses as successful.

evidence_items.explanation: Many prominent benchmarks had flaws that allow inflated scores. One even credits empty responses, which shows gaming can be easy.

receipt.public_excerpt: the ability of these providers to choose the best score leads to biased Arena scores due to selective disclosure of performance results. At an extreme, we identify 27 private LLM variants tested by Meta in the lead-up to the Llama-4 release.

evidence_items.explanation: The leading public leaderboard was distorted by best-of-many private testing, a simple way to game rankings.

receipt.public_excerpt: discovered that every single one can be exploited to achieve near-perfect scores without solving a single task. No reasoning. No capability. Just exploitation of how the score is computed.

evidence_items.explanation: Later confirmation that major benchmarks in use before the post were easy to exploit. It is dated after the post, so it is context only.

unresolved_gaps: No census exists of how many benchmarks are gameable, so 'often' rests on audits of prominent benchmarks rather than a full count.
